Item 5 — Tutorial: Complementary vs. Particular Solutions

Content:
Recall that an inhomogeneous linear system has the form
[MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t),]
where [MATH: A] is a constant matrix and [MATH: \mathbf{g}(t)] is a known forcing term. The associated homogeneous system is
[MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t).]

Content:
A general solution of the homogeneous system is called the complementary solution and is denoted by [MATH: \mathbf{x}_c(t)].
A particular solution is any single function [MATH: \mathbf{x}_p(t)] that satisfies the full inhomogeneous system.

Content:
These two pieces combine to give the general solution of the inhomogeneous system:
[MATH: \mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t)]

Content:
Indeed, notice that
[MATH: (x_{c} + x_{p})^{′}|= x_{c}^{′} + x_{p}^{′}; = (Ax_{c}) + (Ax_{p} + g(t)); = Ax_{c} + Ax_{p} + g(t); = A(x_{c} + x_{p}) + g(t).]
Since [MATH: (\mathbf{x}_c+\mathbf{x}_p)' = A(\mathbf{x}_c+\mathbf{x}_p)+\mathbf{g}(t)], the sum is a solution of the inhomogeneous system.

Content:
Notice that it doesn't matter which particular solution we take.
Suppose we found two different particular solutions, [MATH: \mathbf{x}_p(t)] and [MATH: \mathbf{y}_p(t).] Let's examine their difference, [MATH: \mathbf{w}(t) = \mathbf{y}_p(t) - \mathbf{x}_p(t)].

Content:
By definition, we know that [MATH: \mathbf{y}_p' = A\mathbf{y}_p + \mathbf{g}(t)] and [MATH: \mathbf{x}_p' = A\mathbf{x}_p + \mathbf{g}(t).]
Now, let's find the derivative of the difference [MATH: \mathbf{w}(t)]:
[MATH: w^{′}|= (y_{p} − x_{p})^{′}; = y_{p}^{′} − x_{p}^{′}; = (Ay_{p} + g(t)) − (Ax_{p} + g(t)); = Ay_{p} − Ax_{p}; = A(y_{p} − x_{p}); = Aw]
The result [MATH: \mathbf{w}' = A\mathbf{w}] means that the difference between any two particular solutions is itself a solution to the homogeneous system.

Content:
This is why any particular solution is enough. Any other particular solution can be written as
[MATH: \mathbf{y}_{p} = \underbrace{(\mathbf{y}_{p}-\mathbf{x}_{p})}_{\text{homogeneous}} \:\:\: + \underbrace{\mathbf{x}_{p}}_{\text{particular}} \!\!\!\!\!.]
The "variety" among particular solutions is already captured by the complementary solution [MATH: \mathbf{x}_c(t)].
